subject.title: Background PTY exec runs can survive restart/session loss and become untracked orphan process trees

question: For PTY-backed background exec runs found after gateway restart or lost session state, should OpenClaw kill stale process trees, attempt to reattach/re-register them, or support a narrower hybrid policy?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the behavior affects legitimate long-running work, availability recovery, and operator expectations, so automation should not choose the durable lifecycle policy alone.

options.title: Kill stale PTY trees on startup
options.body: Prefer availability and bounded resource use by treating untracked PTY background runs from an older gateway epoch as stale and terminating their process trees with audit logging.

options.title: Reattach tracked-looking runs
options.body: Persist enough metadata to re-register compatible live PTY runs after restart, accepting more complexity and possible stale-state ambiguity.

options.title: Hybrid with explicit policy
options.body: Kill by default but allow a narrow documented opt-in for reattachable long-running work once maintainers define the public contract.

recommendation.title: Kill stale PTY trees on startup
recommendation.body: Prefer availability and bounded resource use by treating untracked PTY background runs from an older gateway epoch as stale and terminating their process trees with audit logging.
